rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says He will bring after the earlier destroyed peoples their counterparts, such as the Meccan unbelievers.
rows.anchor: نحن { نتبعهم } نظراءهم ككفار مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jussive reading coordinates the verb with We destroy, making the others later destroyed peoples such as Lot, Shuʿayb, and Moses's peoples.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالجزم عطفا على { نهلك } فيكون { الآخرين } المتأخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise means like that act, and the criminals include everyone who commits a crime.
rows.anchor: { كذلك } مثل ذلك الفعل. { نفعل بالمجرمين } بكل من أجرم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers here are those who deny God's signs and messengers.
rows.anchor: بآيات الله وأنبيائه فليس تكريرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first woe concerns the afterlife's punishment, while this one concerns destruction in this world, so it is not redundant.
rows.anchor: لأن ال { ويل } الأول لعذاب الآخرة وهذا للإهلاك في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if both warnings address the same denial, repetition for emphasis is good and common Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: التكرير للتوكيد حسن شائع في كلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lowly fluid is a dirty, base drop of semen.
rows.anchor: نطفة مذرة ذليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure place is the womb.
rows.anchor: هو الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known measure is the period God appointed until birth.
rows.anchor: إلى مقدار معلوم من الوقت قدره الله تعالى للولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean that God was able to do this, or that He determined it.
rows.anchor: على ذلك، أو فقدرناه ويدل عليه قراءة نافع

rows.speaker: نافع والكسائي
rows.claim: Nafiʿ and al-Kisaʾi read the verb with shadda, supporting the sense that God determined it.
rows.anchor: قراءة نافع والكسائي بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise means that God is fully able to carry out what He determined.
rows.anchor: { فنعم القدرون } نحن. { ويل يومئذ للمكذبين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers reject God's power to create this way or to resurrect.
rows.anchor: بقدرتنا على ذلك أو على الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is split open.
rows.anchor: وشققت وقرأ الكوفيون بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans read the verb in its lighter form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky becomes like all doors because of its many splits, or it becomes a thing with doors.
rows.anchor: من كثرة الشقوق كأن الكل أبواب أو فصارت ذات أبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains move through the air like scattered dust and become mirages, retaining an apparent mountain shape after their substance crumbles and disperses.
rows.anchor: وسيرت الجبال } أي في الهواء كالهباء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes Hell a place where its keepers lie in wait for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: موضع رصد يرصد فيه خزنة النار الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, keepers of Paradise guard believers from Hell's heat as they pass over it.
rows.anchor: أو خزنة الجنة المؤمنين ليحرسوهم من فيحها في مجازهم عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word may evoke a place where horses are conditioned, or a vigilant ambush for unbelievers so none escapes, like a fierce attacker.
rows.anchor: كالمضمار فإنه الموضع الذي تضمر فيه الخيل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading إن with fatḥa makes the clause causal, explaining why the Hour is established.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { أن } بالفتح على التعليل لقيام الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the rebels, Hell is a return and dwelling place.
rows.anchor: مرجعا ومأوى

rows.speaker: حمزة وروح
rows.claim: Hamza and Rawh read labithin, which is more emphatic.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وروح «لبثين» وهو أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word means successive stretches of ages.
rows.anchor: { أحقابا } دهورا متتابعة، وليس فيها ما يدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not establish that unbelievers leave Hell: even if an age is eighty years or seventy thousand years, ages can recur without end.
rows.anchor: فليس فيه ما يتقضى تناهي تلك الأحقاب لجواز أن يكون المراد أحقابا مترادفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even an inference that the ages end is only implicit meaning and cannot outweigh the explicit proof that unbelievers remain forever.
rows.anchor: فمن قبيل المفهوم فلا يعارض المنطق الدال على خلود الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is understood as introducing quoted speech: Go to Pharaoh, [and say these words].
rows.anchor: { اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى } على إرادة القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative reading أن أذهب reflects the meaning of speech already contained in the address.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «أن أذهب» لما في النداء من معنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks whether Pharaoh is inclined to purify himself from disbelief and rebellion.
rows.anchor: هل لك ميل إلى أن تتطهر من الكفر والطغيان

rows.speaker: الحجازيان ويعقوب
rows.claim: The Hijazis and Yaqub read the verb with shadda.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحجازيان ويعقوب« تزكى » بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses offers to guide Pharaoh to know God, so that he will fear Him by doing duties and leaving prohibitions; fear follows knowledge.
rows.anchor: { فتخشى } بأداء الواجبات وترك المحرمات، إذ الخشية إنما تكون بعد المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This offer to speak gently spells out the instruction to use gentle words with Pharaoh.
rows.anchor:
فقولا له قولا لينا
[طه: 44]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest sign may be the staff turning into a serpent, as the first and central miracle, or all his miracles considered one sign because of their shared proof.
rows.anchor: فذهب وبلغ فأراه المعجزة الكبرى وهي قلب العصا حية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the sign appeared and the matter was established, Pharaoh denied Moses and disobeyed God.
rows.anchor: فكذب موسى وعصى الله عز وجل بعد ظهور الآية وتحقق الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned from obedience and strove to undo Moses's mission, or fled in terror after seeing the serpent.
rows.anchor: عن الطاعة. { يسعى } ساعيا في إبطال أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat Abasa is Meccan and has forty-two verses.
rows.anchor: مكية وآيها ثنتان وأربعون آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet was inviting Quraysh leaders to Islam, repeatedly asked to be taught, and the Prophet frowned and turned away; revelation followed. The Prophet later welcomed and honored him and appointed him over Medina twice; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: أن ابن أم مكتوم أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنده صناديد قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A doubled reading intensifies the sense of frowning.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «عبس» بالتشديد للمبالغة و { أن جاءه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may give the cause of turning away or of frowning, depending on the grammatical analysis.
rows.anchor: { أن جاءه } علة ل { تولى } ، أو { عبس } على اختلاف المذهبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with two hamzas and an alif between them asks, Was it because the blind man came that he did this?
rows.anchor: وقرىء «آأن» بهمزتين وبألف بينهما بمعنى ألئن جاءه الأعمى فعل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning his blindness can excuse his interruption and show that he especially deserved compassion, or heighten the rebuke as if to ask whether the Prophet turned away because he was blind.
rows.anchor: وذكر الأعمى للإشعار بعذره في الإقدام على قطع كلام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means, how could you know his state? He may purify himself from sins by what he learns from you; this hints that the Prophet turned away to help another become purified.
rows.anchor: وأي شيء يجعلك داريا بحاله لعله يتطهر من الآثام بما يتلقف منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man may take heed and benefit from the Prophet's admonition.
rows.anchor: أو يتعظ فتنفعه موعظتك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the pronoun refer to the unbeliever: the Prophet hoped to purify and admonish him by conversion, and so turned from the other man, though success was uncertain.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير في { لعله } للكافر أي أنك طمعت في تزكيه

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim reads the verb in the subjunctive as a result clause after laʿalla.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم فتنفعه بالنصب جوابا للعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person regards himself as self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: { أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى } تتعرض له بالإقبال عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means you attend to him; its underlying form is tataṣaddā.
rows.anchor: تتعرض له بالإقبال عليه وأصله تتصدى

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Nafi read the form with assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع «تصدى» بالإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading can mean either that you turn toward him or that you are summoned to attend to him.
rows.anchor: وقرىء. «تصدى» أي تعرض وتدعى إلى التصدي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not accountable if the man does not convert; eagerness for his Islam should not cause neglect of one who has accepted it.
rows.anchor: وليس عليك بأس في أن لا يتزكى بالإسلام حتى يبعثك الحرص على إسلامه إلى الإعراض عمن أسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point agrees with the statement that the Messenger's duty is only to convey the message.
rows.anchor: إن عليك إلا البلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the person who comes swiftly seeking good.
rows.anchor: يسرع طالبا للخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are honored by God, or kind toward believers by speaking to them and seeking forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: أعزاء على الله أو متعطفين على المؤمنين يكلمونهم ويستغفرون لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term means pious.
rows.anchor: ويستغفرون لهم. { بررة } أتقياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This curses humanity in the harshest terms and expresses astonishment at its extreme ingratitude; its brevity conveys intense anger and blame.
rows.anchor: دعاه عليه بأشنع الدعوات وتعجب من إفراطه في الكفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question recalls God's particular favor in bringing the person into existence.
rows.anchor: بيان لما أنعم عليه خصوصا من مبدأ حدوثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question belittles the human origin, which the following verse answers.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام للتحقير ولذلك أجاب عنه بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepared the person for fitting organs and forms, or determined his successive developmental stages until his creation was complete.
rows.anchor: فهيأه لما يصلح له من الأعضاء والأشكال،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God eased the person's exit from his mother's womb by opening the womb and inspiring him to turn headfirst, or made the path of good and evil easy for him.
rows.anchor: ثم سهل مخرجه من بطن أمه بأن فتح فوهة الرحم وألهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative is governed by a verb explained by the following verb, intensifying the sense of ease.
rows.anchor: ونصب السبيل بفعل يفسره الظاهر للمبالغة في التيسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the definite article rather than a possessive construction signals a path common to all.
rows.anchor: وتعريفه باللام دون الإضافة للإشعار بأنه سبيل عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the moral-path reading, the verse hints that worldly life is a road whose destination lies elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وفيه على المعنى الأخير إيماء بأن الدنيا طريق والمقصد غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat al-Infitar is Meccan and has nineteen verses.
rows.anchor: مكية وآيها تسع عشرة آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky splits open.
rows.anchor: إذا السماء انفطرت } انشقت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars fall scattered apart.
rows.anchor: الكواكب انتثرت } تساقطت متفرقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seas are opened into one another until they become one sea.
rows.anchor: فتح بعضها إلى بعض فصار الكل بحرا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The graves are overturned, their soil stirred, and their dead brought out.
rows.anchor: قلب ترابها وأخرج موتاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One etymology treats the word as a compound of baʿth and athāra, like basmala; bahthara is a parallel in form and meaning.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه مركب من بعث وراء الإثارة كبسمل ونظيره بحثر لفظا ومعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What a person sent ahead may be deeds or charity, while what was left behind may be sins or neglected duties.
rows.anchor: من عمل أو صدقة. { وأخرت } من سيئة أو تركت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, delayed means squandered.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالتأخير التضييع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about what each soul did is the answer to when.
rows.anchor: وهو جواب { إذا }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what deceived and emboldened a person to disobey; calling God generous is meant to deter presumption, since generosity does not require neglecting wrongdoers or equating obedient and disobedient people.
rows.anchor: أي شيء خدعك وجرأك على عصيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording exposes Satan's false reassurance that one may do as one pleases because a generous Lord neither punishes nor hastens punishment.
rows.anchor: فإنه يقول له افعل ما شئت فربك كريم لا يعذب أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's great generosity calls for earnest obedience, not immersion in sin under the illusion that grace makes it safe.
rows.anchor: كثرة كرمه تستدعي الجد في طاعته لا الانهماك في عصيانه اغترارا بكرمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This second description of the Lord confirms His lordship, manifests His generosity, and shows that the One able to create first can create again.
rows.anchor: صفة ثانية مقررة للربوبية مبينة للكرم منبهة على أن من قدر على ذلك أولا قدر عليه ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To form soundly is to make the organs healthy, proportioned, and ready for their uses.
rows.anchor: جعل الأعضاء سليمة مسواة معدة لمنافعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adjustment may mean making the bodily structure and organs proportionate, or balancing it with faculties that bring felicity.
rows.anchor: جعل البنية معدلة متناسبة الأعضاء،

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans read the verb lightly, meaning either that the limbs balance one another or that God distinguished the person from other creatures by his form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون «فعدلك» بالتخفيف أي عدل بعض أعضائك ببعض حتى اعتدلت

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means God formed the person in whichever form He chose; ma may be extra or conditional, with rakabaka as its answer.
rows.anchor: أي ركبك في أي صورة شاءها، و { ما } مزيدة وقيل شرطية، و { ركبك } جوابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase attaches to adalaka.
rows.anchor: و الظرف صلة { عدلك } ، وإنما لم يعطف الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This sentence explains the preceding word adalaka, which is why it is not coordinated with the preceding sentence.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يعطف الجملة على ما قبلها لأنها بيان لعدلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This rebukes people for presuming on God's generosity.
rows.anchor: ردع عن الاغترار بكرم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The turn identifies the real cause of their presumption: they deny the recompense, or deny Islam.
rows.anchor: إضراب إلى بيان ما هو السبب الأصلي في اغترارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closest servants drink Tasnim unmixed because they have occupied themselves only with God.
rows.anchor: فإنهم يشربونها صرفا لأنهم لم يشتغلوا بغير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasnim is mixed for the other inhabitants of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وتمزج لسائر أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative may be for praise or a circumstantial accusative from Tasnim.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب { عينا } على المدح أو الحال { من تسنيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion of the preposition here is the same as for the phrase about God's servants drinking by it.
rows.anchor: والكلام في الباء كما في يشرب بها عباد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinners are the leaders of Quraysh, who mocked poor believers.
rows.anchor: يعني رؤساء قريش. { كانوا من الذين ءامنوا يضحكون } كانوا يستهزئون بفقراء المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They gestured to one another with their eyes.
rows.anchor: بهم يتغامزون } يغمز بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They returned home taking pleasure in their mockery.
rows.anchor: منهم، وقرأ حفص «فكهين»

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads the word with this form, fakihin.
rows.anchor: منهم، وقرأ حفص «فكهين»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the mockers saw the believers, they labeled them misguided.
rows.anchor: وإذا رأوا المؤمنين نسبوهم إلى الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mockers were not appointed as guardians over believers to assess their deeds or certify their guidance and error.
rows.anchor: على المؤمنين. { حفظين } يحفظون عليهم أعمالهم ويشهدون برشدهم وضلالهم.

words: إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes the person meet his own effort; toil is strenuous work that leaves a mark, from the verb meaning to scratch.
rows.anchor: وتقديره لاقى الإنسان كدحه أي جهدا يؤثر فيه من كدحه إذا خدشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the person meets God, while the statement that he toils toward his Lord is parenthetical; his toil is pursuit of the meeting with his recompense.
rows.anchor: والكدح إليه السعي إلى لقاء جزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An easy reckoning is one in which the person is not cross-examined.
rows.anchor: سهلا لا يناقش فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His family may be his believing relatives, the community of believers, or his family in Paradise among the houris.
rows.anchor: إلى عشيرته المؤمنين، أو فريق المؤمنين، أو { أهله } في الجنة من الحور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving the book behind his back means receiving it in his left hand from behind.
rows.anchor: أي يؤتى كتابه بشماله من وراء ظهره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says the right hand is tied to the neck and the left hand placed behind the back.
rows.anchor: قيل تغل يمناه إلى عنقه وتجعل يسراه وراء ظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will wish for destruction and cry, O my destruction; thubur means ruin.
rows.anchor: يتمنى الثبور ويقول يا ثبوراه وهو الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He enters the blazing Fire.
rows.anchor: ويصلى سعيرا

rows.speaker: الحجازيان والشامي
rows.claim: The Hijazis and the Shami read this verb in the form supported by the parallel phrase in 56:94.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحجازيان والشامي «ويصلى» لقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is supported by the parallel wording in 4:115.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «ويصلى» لقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This answers the preceding question; the fluid is one that gushes forcefully, and means the mixture of two fluids in the womb.
rows.anchor: وهو صعب فيه دفع والمراد الممتزج من الماءين في الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression means fluid possessing a forceful gush.
rows.anchor: بمعنى ذي دفق، وهو صعب فيه دفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms refer to the man's backbone and the woman's chest bones.
rows.anchor: من بين صلب الرجل وترائب المرأة وهي عظام صدرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the conditional medical account that semen derives from the fourth digestion and separates from all organs, the brain greatly assists its production; the semen resembles it and excessive intercourse weakens it.
rows.anchor: فلا شك أن الدماغ أعظم الأعضاء معونة في توليدها، ولذلك تشبهه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word has readings with fatḥatayn or ḍammatayn, and a fourth dialect form ṣālib.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «الصلب» بفتحتين و « الصلب» بضمتين وفيه لغة رابعة وهي «صالب».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Creator, as indicated by the earlier mention of creation.
rows.anchor: والضمير للخالق ويدل عليه { خلق }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day secrets are exposed, distinguishing sound intentions and hidden deeds from corrupt ones; the phrase is a time adverb linked to His return of the person.
rows.anchor: تتعرف ويميز بين ما طاب من الضمائر وما خفي من الأعمال وما خبث منها

words: فَمَا لَهُ مِن قُوَّةٍ وَلَا نَاصِرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person has no inner power to protect himself and no helper to protect him.
rows.anchor: { فما له } فما للإنسان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the sky repeatedly returns to the place from which it moves in each cycle.
rows.anchor: ترجع في كل دورة إلى الموضع الذي تتحرك عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-rajʿ is rain, named for its repeated return at intervals.
rows.anchor: وقيل الرجع المطر سمي به كما سمي أوبا لأن الله يرجعه وقتا فوقتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that clouds carry water from the seas and return it to the earth; on this reading, sky may mean cloud.
rows.anchor: لما قيل من أن السحاب يحمل الماء من البحار ثم يرجعه إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's cleaving may refer to plants emerging from it, or to the cracks produced by plants and springs.
rows.anchor: ما تتصدع عنه الأرض من النبات أو الشق بالنبات والعيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a decisive statement that separates truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: { إنه } إن القرآن. { لقول فصل } فاصل بين الحق والباطل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an contains nothing frivolous; it is wholly serious.
rows.anchor: فإنه جد كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the people of Mecca, plotting to invalidate the Qur'an and extinguish its light.
rows.anchor: يعني أهل مكة. { يكيدون كيدا } في إبطاله وإطفاء نوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God counters their plot by drawing them on and taking vengeance from where they do not expect it.
rows.anchor: وأقابلهم بكيد في استدراجي لهم وانتقامي منهم من حيث لا يحتسبون
